hook: the Chmielnicki uprising destroys Jewish communities in Ukraine
carry: a number that stands for real people

segments.voice: Yesterday, England readmitted Jews, not by law but through a door left unlocked. Your line was readmitted. A new week begins far to the east, with a hard memory. Go gently today.

Jewish memory has its own way of naming years. In the Hebrew calendar, years are written with letters, and two short letter-words, tach and tat, came to stand for a time of terror in Poland and Ukraine. Jews spoke of the decrees of tach and tat the way other people say a date they cannot forget. In the ordinary calendar, the first of those years is a single number, and it is today's title.
screen: `YEARS WRITTEN IN LETTERS.` → `TACH AND TAT.` → `A NUMBER THAT IS A MEMORY.`

segments.voice: In the lands of Ukraine then ruled by Poland, the Cossacks rose up under a leader named Bohdan Chmielnicki. The uprising had its own grievances, against Polish lords and their power over the land and the people who worked it. Jews were caught in the middle. Some served the lords as stewards and leaseholders, collecting rents and running mills and inns, so in the rebels' eyes they stood for the lords. As the rebels moved through the towns, Jewish communities were attacked and destroyed. People fled to fortified towns, and some of those towns fell. Families were killed, taken captive, or forced to convert. The chronicles give large numbers, and historians still argue over them. What no one disputes is that whole communities disappeared. A survivor named Nathan Hannover wrote a chronicle of those years, in plain Hebrew, town by town, so people would know. He took its title from a drowning cry in the Psalms: "I am sunk in deep mire, where there is no standing." Deep mire, in Hebrew, is yeven metzulah. Afterward, the rabbis of Poland set aside a day of fasting and lament, and some communities kept it long afterward. A massacre in these lessons is not a plot twist. It is a number that stands for real people, names mostly lost, held in a people's memory. That is what 1648 means here.
screen: `AN UPRISING AGAINST POLISH LORDS.` · `JEWS CAUGHT IN THE MIDDLE.` · `WHOLE COMMUNITIES DESTROYED.` · `DEEP MIRE, WHERE THERE IS NO STANDING.` · then, large: `1648.`

segments.voice: Sit still and let your hands rest open; there's no need to picture anything violent. Just hold in mind that there were towns, and in them families, someone baking bread, a child learning letters, an old man at prayer, and let the silence be for them. If you pray, you can remember them in your own words, or with no words at all.
Yeven metzulah. Deep mire, the name a survivor gave his chronicle of 1648, when Jewish communities in Ukraine were destroyed. Today's word.
Your line: a number that stands for real people. Their names are mostly lost; the memory is not. See you tomorrow.
